headline: AI models are 'drifting' – losing skills in unexpected areas, research shows
summary: Researchers from Stanford and UC Berkeley confirm "Model Drift," where AI models degrade in some areas after being retrained for others, affecting LLMs like Gemini and ChatGPT.
details: Developers are noticing a decline in AI model performance, with LLMs like Gemini and ChatGPT failing at tasks they once handled easily. This phenomenon, dubbed "Model Drift," suggests AI models aren't static but can degrade over time.

Part of the perceived decline is due to increased user expectations. The initial "wow" effect has worn off, and users now challenge models with complex edge cases, viewing previous "impressive attempts" as failures.

Constant updates for safety and alignment also contribute. Over-correcting for safety can lead to "over-refusal" or bland, cautious responses, making models seem less capable in complex coding or nuanced arguments.

Cost and speed optimizations also play a role. Companies use techniques like quantization (compressing models) and Mixture of Experts (routing queries to smaller sub-models) to handle millions of users. This optimization can sometimes prioritize speed over cognitive depth.

Stanford and UC Berkeley researchers have documented that retraining models to improve specific skills, such as preventing toxic output or fixing a niche bug, can unexpectedly degrade performance in unrelated areas like math logic or code generation. This creates a "whack-a-mole" scenario for engineers.

headline_marked: [[Putin casts online vote using unlicensed Windows]] on an American Dell PC
headline: Putin casts online vote using unlicensed Windows on an American Dell PC
summary: An official Kremlin video shows President Putin voting online with an 'Activate Windows' watermark visible, using a foreign Dell PC despite Russian tech mandates.
details: Russian President Vladimir Putin participated in online State Duma elections, with an official Kremlin video showing him using an unlicensed copy of Windows on a Dell PC. A prominent 'Activate Windows' watermark was visible on the screen during the filmed event.

The watermark, similar to Windows activation reminders, was confirmed by several established Russian media sources like Komsomolskaya Pravda. Another overlay on the screen was dated 2018, though the activation reminder appeared current.

TASS reported that Putin has preferred remote voting in recent years for the election of deputies to the 9th State Duma. The vote also included residents from recently incorporated Ukrainian territories for the first time.

Social media users highlighted the irony of Putin's comment 'You can't go wrong' while clicking his candidate, given the predictable nature of Russian election results. The ruling United Russia party, backed by Putin, is widely expected to perform well.

The use of a foreign-branded Dell computer also drew attention, as Russian law mandates officials use localized computers. This suggests the machine might have been specifically set up for the publicity clip, potentially explaining the unactivated Windows.

Observations were also made regarding Putin's mouse skills, with some attributing his hesitant interactions to difficulty seeing the screen. Suggestions were made for him to wear glasses or for administrators to adjust the display.
